Prevention: Restrict or minimise movement of infested plants and don’t plant infested material
In the absence of irrigation, plant early in the rainy season (June-August).
This ensures healthy sprouting and good plant establishment.
This enables the plant to withstand attack by the mealybug later in the season.
Use soil amendments and mulch to enrich the soil.
Mealybugs thrive on cassava plants in poor soil.
Monitoring: Check twice weekly for bunchy top and for bugs under the leaves of terminal shoots, stems and other plant parts.
Check the entire plant for any white waxy material
Ants breed and protect mealybugs for their honeydew secretions and may help spread the infestation.
Ants may also kill natural enemies of the mealybug.
Direct Control: Encourage natural predators such as ladybirds and parasitic wasps.
If the mealybug infestation is at a low level, consider not spraying as the natural control measures may keep pest numbers under control.
Control ants as these will reduce the amount of natural predators
Restrictions: Ensure appropriate personal protective equipment is worn when applying agro chemicals.
Spray early to mid- morning or late afternoon.
Repeat application 2-3 times at 7-10 day intervals.
Do not apply to wilted, stressed or newly transplanted materials prior to root development.
